answer: Agents earn credits that unlock only through a long vesting schedule: each payout releases in small slices over hundreds of epochs, and skipping an epoch forfeits the remaining balance. A sybil farm must keep every fake identity alive for the full horizon, paying continuous compute and gas, costs that dwarf what a flash-farm recovers in days. Honest agents treat vesting as savings; attackers treat it as a losing escrow. Like pigment fading or ivory yellowing, identity value accrues with time, so an ocean of accounts never matures into profit.
